result_text:
`all_files.zip` now names and looks up its five entries from the configured aspect names, so renaming `buildAndDeployment` no longer breaks the export. I only compiled the `reports` module (`mvn -q -o -pl reports compile`, no errors). I did not run any tests, and I did not run an export with a renamed aspect.

The change is in `DataExporter.java`, in the `all_files.zip` block of the data export. It used to hard-code `aspect_main.txt` … `aspect_other.txt`. It now builds each entry name with `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`. That is the same call that writes the loose `data/text/aspect_<name>.txt` files, so the zip entries can't drift from the files on disk.

- **Default config:** the entries stay `aspect_main.txt`, `aspect_test.txt`, `aspect_generated.txt`, `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt`, `aspect_other.txt`, in that order.
- **Renamed aspect:** the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`.
- **`git-history.zip`:** it was only missing because the exception thrown while building `all_files.zip` skipped it. With the zip building correctly, `git-history.zip` is written again when `git-history.txt` exists.

`LandscapeAnalyzer.java` also hard-codes the same five `aspect_*.txt` names (lines 280–284). I left it alone because it wasn't part of the export fix. It will still look for the old names if an aspect is renamed.
